## Summary

I created two JUnit test classes matching the project's existing conventions (JUnit 3.8.2, `junit.framework.TestCase`, `testXxx()` methods, `try { ...; fail(); } catch (X expected) {}` for exception assertions):

- **`gson/src/test/java/com/google/gson/stream/JsonReaderAgentTest.java`** (46 tests) — covers construction/NPE, lenient toggling, array/object reading, every `JsonToken` returned by `peek()`, all `nextXxx()` accessors (string/boolean/null/double/long/int) including their type-mismatch and overflow errors, strict-vs-lenient parsing of malformed constructs (leading zeros, single-quoted/unquoted strings, comments, multiple top-level values, non-execute prefix), `skipValue()` over scalars/arrays/nested structures, `close()` behavior (closes the underlying `Reader`, disables further reads), `getPath()`, and `toString()`.
- **`gson/src/test/java/com/google/gson/stream/JsonWriterAgentTest.java`** (39 tests) — covers construction/NPE, default flag values and setters, writing every scalar type (including `BigInteger`/`BigDecimal`), string escaping (control chars, quotes, HTML-safe mode), `setIndent` pretty-printing, `serializeNulls` behavior for object members vs. array elements, `name()` error cases (null, dangling, outside object, after close), nesting-mismatch errors, `close()`/`flush()` semantics (incomplete document, closed-state errors), and multiple-top-level-value handling under strict/lenient modes.

While probing edge cases, I discovered (by reading the actual `JsonWriter.value(double)` source, not assumption) that this checkout's `value(double)` rejects NaN/Infinity **unconditionally**, even in lenient mode — unlike `value(Number)`, which does respect the lenient flag. I wrote the tests to assert that real, verified behavior rather than the "expected" textbook behavior. Similarly, `JsonReader` silently returns `END_DOCUMENT` from `peek()` after a top-level scalar is already consumed instead of throwing `EOFException` (which only fires on a genuinely empty stream) — tests assert that actual behavior too.

**Verification:**
```
defects4j compile
→ Running ant (compile)...OK / Running ant (compile.tests)...OK

java -cp "$(defects4j export -p cp.test)" org.junit.runner.JUnitCore \
  com.google.gson.stream.JsonReaderAgentTest com.google.gson.stream.JsonWriterAgentTest
→ OK (85 tests)
```

No files other than the two new test classes were created or modified.
